data.narrative:
Bethlehem Steel Corp is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $690M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 9 peers—1 public and 8 private companies including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics—though narrow peer matching constraints limit applicability of certain methods.

Stage-progression analysis, the primary applicable method, applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier to the $690M total raised proxy, reflecting typical valuation expansion from Growth stage to the next progression phase. This yields an implied valuation of $828M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Robotics & Manufacturing sector; the 10 total sector peers lack sufficient clustering to support robust median-based inference without introducing undue noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $704M to $952M, with a median of $828M, supported by one substantive method. The wide band reflects the inherent uncertainty when relying on stage-based mechanics without corroborating peer multiples. Key unknowns include whether true comparable transactions exist at tighter valuation proximity, whether the 1.2x multiplier appropriately captures this company's risk and growth trajectory relative to the broader cohort, and whether additional private comp data would materially narrow the range. Management should be prepared to support claims about relative competitive positioning that would justify positioning within this range.
